entities.name: Mirrodin
entities.description: The metal plane whose nonhuman and human cultures, called Mirrans, are described in the Scars of Mirrodin style guide.

entities.name: Phyrexia
entities.description: Invader whose incursion is beginning to change Mirrodin's cultures before a full-scale planar war.

entities.name: Leonin
entities.description: Proud, fierce, lion-like humanoids, the most advanced and organized race of the Razor Fields.

entities.name: Kha-Tal
entities.description: The leonin pride loyal to the authority of the kha, led by Kemba as Regent.

entities.name: Obu-Tal
entities.description: A smaller pride of young leonin rebels who blame the Kha-Tal and seek a new society, led by Juryan.

entities.name: Kemba
entities.description: Young leonin skyhunter and hero chosen as popular leader and Regent in Raksha's absence; she rebuilt Taj-Nar.

entities.name: Raksha Golden Cub
entities.description: The leonin kha who disappeared with the elder generation.

entities.name: Juryan
entities.description: Ferocious, charismatic young leader of the rebel Obu-Tal, who wants revolution and a new leonin society.

entities.name: Memnarch
entities.description: Former ruler of Mirrodin whose ascendancy, war and fall shaped the plane; his soul traps were destroyed.

entities.name: Sun's Toll
entities.description: The event that caused the world's elder generations to disappear.

entities.name: Taj-Nar
entities.description: The ancient leonin den and capitol, nearly destroyed by a mana bomb in the war with Memnarch and since rebuilt.

entities.name: Regent's Guard
entities.description: Elite force of leonin warriors, mages and skyhunters defending Taj-Nar.

entities.name: Razor Fields
entities.description: Region of Mirrodin inhabited by leonin and loxodons.

entities.name: Loxodons
entities.description: Elephant humanoids of the Razor Fields, formidable warriors with unswerving beliefs.

entities.name: Modest Truth
entities.description: The collective loxodon rules and religion, passed from generation to generation.

entities.name: Ghalma
entities.description: Loxodon woman who shapes metal like liquid without a forge, sought by Neurok artificers.

entities.name: Neurok
entities.description: Artificers who hope to use Ghalma's talent to create new synthetic life.

entities.name: Vedalken
entities.description: Knowledge-driven race pursuing the Origin Query, whose rule was solidified by Memnarch's fall.

entities.name: Origin Query
entities.description: The question of the origin of the vedalken race that drives their pursuit of knowledge.

entities.name: Synod
entities.description: Vedalken ruling body that alone had a full view of ascertained knowledge; it later fell.

entities.name: Sanctives
entities.description: Seven vedalken factions formed to codify and compartmentalize knowledge.

entities.name: Knowledge Pool
entities.description: Sacred vedalken bank of knowledge whose destabilization is their greatest secret.

entities.name: Nim
entities.description: Mirrodin's undead, ravenous zombies created by necrogen with metal evolutions.

entities.name: Mephidross
entities.description: Swamp analog of Mirrodin that hums with a dissonant chord and whose chimneys emit necrogen.

entities.name: Necrogen
entities.description: Sickly green gas emitted by the chimneys of the Dross that turns creatures into nim.

entities.name: Goblins
entities.description: Unified, partly metal goblins with their own cosmology and thing-making craft.

entities.name: Steel Mother
entities.description: What goblins believe Mirrodin itself to be, the entity that created them.

entities.name: Sky Tyrant
entities.description: The red sun, believed by goblins to be the hammer that forged the Steel Mother.

entities.name: Ugly Child
entities.description: Goblin name for the green sun, a homely cosmic brother.

entities.name: Great Furnace
entities.description: Goblin furnace where dead goblins' metal is melted down and offerings are cast.

entities.name: Viridian elves
entities.description: Surviving Tangle elves who turned anti-technology and militant after the Vanishing.

entities.name: Ezuri
entities.description: Charismatic leader of the Viridian Resurgents.

entities.name: Vanishing
entities.description: The disappearance of many of Mirrodin's original inhabitants after Memnarch's soul traps were destroyed.

entities.name: Tel-Jilad Chosen
entities.description: Hierarchy around which Viridian elf society was ordered before the Fifth Dawn.

entities.name: Tangle
entities.description: Forest region of Mirrodin, home of elves, whose population was decimated by the Vanishing.

entities.name: Cambree Garden
entities.description: Largest fortified garden in the Tangle, built around a field of gelfruit.

events.summary: After the Sun's Toll the unified leonin pride fractures into the Kha-Tal and the rebel Obu-Tal.
events.quote: Mirrodin's unified pride of leonin fractured into two smaller prides.

events.summary: Kemba, who led hundreds of leonin to safety during Memnarch's ascendancy, is chosen as popular leader and takes the title Regent rather than kha.
events.quote: Kemba refused to take the title kha, preferring to be known as "Regent,"

events.summary: Kemba oversees the reconstruction of Taj-Nar.
events.quote: Kemba has overseen the reconstruction of Taj-Nar

events.summary: Juryan's scouts capture a strange creature whose metal and flesh are fused, which may become his weapon against the Kha-Tal.
events.quote: his scouts discovered and captured a strange, new kind of creature

events.summary: Taj-Nar's tower was nearly destroyed with a mana bomb during the war with Memnarch.
events.quote: was almost totally destroyed with a mana bomb during the war with Memnarch.

events.summary: Taj-Nar is rebuilt with greater defenses and the Regent's Guard is created.
events.quote: Taj-Nar has been painstakingly rebuilt, but with greater magical defenses.

events.summary: Neurok artificers seek out Ghalma's gift to create synthetic life.
events.quote: Neurok artificers who hope to use her talent to create new forms of synthetic life have sought her gift out.

events.summary: Memnarch falls, solidifying vedalken rule and prompting unchecked vedalken experimentation.
events.quote: Vedalken rule was solidified by the fall of Memnarch.

events.summary: The vedalken form the seven Sanctives to control knowledge.
events.quote: For this purpose the seven Sanctives were formed.

events.summary: Vedalken experiments devastate the blinkmoth population, making serum extremely rare.
events.quote: This myopic and uncontrolled research soon made blinkmoths, and thus serum, among the rarest commodities on Mirrodin.

events.summary: The Knowledge Pool destabilizes and goes insane, a secret the vedalken keep even through the Synod's fall.
Necrogen from the Dross chimneys transforms creatures into nim.
With Memnarch's soul traps destroyed, many Mirrodin inhabitants vanish and the elves' culture nearly collapses.
events.quote: After Memnarch's soul traps were destroyed, many of Mirrodin's original inhabitants disappeared from Mirrodin.

events.summary: Under Ezuri the Viridian Resurgents embark on a mission to destroy the myr, vedalken and anything unnatural.
events.quote: Under the leadership of the charismatic Ezuri, they embark on a mission to destroy the myr, the vedalken, and anything else they deem unnatural.

events.summary: The Viridians reject the Tel-Jilad hierarchy and form voluntary brigades called gades.
events.quote: Once the Viridians rejected the hierarchy of the Tel-Jilad, they organized themselves into voluntary brigades.

relations.quote: was chosen as the leonin's popular leader.

relations.note: Led the Obu-Tal to break away
relations.quote: who led the Obu-Tal to break off from the main pride of leonin
Juryan's warriors have been fighting off Kha-Tal loyalists over land and resources
Under the leadership of the charismatic Ezuri

relations.note: Resurgents target the vedalken as unnatural
relations.quote: They see the vedalken's experimentation- and knowledge-driven society as a destructive force
the leonin kha, Raksha Golden Cub, disappeared with them.
